title: serve s3 uses too much memory on multipart uploads
body: When uploading multipart files, `serve s3` holds all the parts in memory. This is a documented limitation of the library rclone uses for serving S3.

symptoms_visible: When I upload multipart files through `rclone serve s3`, all of the parts remain in memory.
N0.label: N0 multipart memory issue reported

symptoms_visible: Multipart uploads through `serve s3` retain all uploaded parts in memory.
N1.label: N1 implementation constraints identified

symptoms_visible: With the first candidate container, our roughly 300 MB backup raises container memory usage to about 640 MiB and the container still crashes when limited to 400 MiB.
N2.label: N2 initial candidate still consumes upload-sized memory

symptoms_visible: With `GOGC=20`, `--use-mmap`, and `--max-buffer-memory=200`, memory still reaches about 640 MiB.
With those settings and a 400 MiB container limit, the container fills its memory and fails.
The backup client sends the roughly 290 MB backup as 14 parts using two workers.
N2_x.label: N2_x memory-control probe results

symptoms_visible: The candidate build still reaches about 640 MiB while `serve s3` writes through my `crypted` remote to Ceph RGW.
N3.label: N3 crypt-wrapped backend configuration established

symptoms_visible: The next candidate fails on the first multipart upload with `crypt: partEncrypter unsupported seek` and then reports that overlapping multipart parts must all have the same size except for the last part.
N4.label: N4 crypt-specific candidate error

symptoms_visible: With the simplified candidate, the same backup has a much smaller memory imprint.
A 2 GiB upload through the encryption proxy completes with client upload concurrency one or two, including with our normal server configuration.
The source and destination both report MD5 `7e1e0c88057047b9d4912dc409a8e55f`.
N5.label: N5 simplified candidate verified

symptoms_visible: Multipart uploads through the S3 encryption proxy complete with a much smaller memory imprint, and the uploaded data has the same MD5 checksum as the source.
N_terminal.label: terminal multipart memory fix verified

question_patterns: What implementation options are available, and what trade-offs do they have across different backends?
Could multipart parts be stored outside memory, or sent onward incrementally?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I see three options. `--vfs-cache-mode writes` could assemble the file on local disk and upload it when finished, but it needs disk space and delays the upload until the end. Storing each part separately would require joining the chunks again on download. For backends supporting `OpenChunkWriter` or `OpenWriterAt`, I originally planned to send chunks directly to the backend, though that would not work for backends without those interfaces.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The destination backend cannot accept incremental or random-access writes, and local disk buffering is the only permitted storage option.
Local disk buffering is available, but direct backend multipart handling is preferred to avoid delaying the upload.

edges.comment: From c1-c2: participant2 identified gofakes3's in-memory `Body` field, and reporter ncw described the disk-cache, separate-part, and direct-backend alternatives. The contributor and reporter are folded into one technical user side.

question_patterns: Please run the provided candidate container with your normal multipart backup and report its memory usage.
Could you test the candidate under your usual workload and under a 400 MiB container limit?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried the linked candidate in our dev environment. Our roughly 300 MB backup makes the container use about 640 MiB. With the container limited to 400 MiB, it reaches the limit and crashes just as before.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same backup stays below 100 MiB and completes under the 400 MiB limit.
The peak is about 610 MiB rather than 640 MiB, and it still exceeds the 400 MiB limit.

edges.comment: From c6-c9: reporter ncw supplied the first candidate and affected operator linwalth tested it in a development container. This is a pre-landing build measurement, so the users are folded into one simulated side and the edge changes knowledge rather than the retained system.

question_patterns: Can you rerun it with `GOGC=20`, `--use-mmap`, and a `--max-buffer-memory` cap and report the observed memory usage?
Please try the garbage-collection and buffer controls under the 400 MiB container limit and tell me what the process does.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried `GOGC=20`, `--use-mmap`, and `--max-buffer-memory=200`. The process still reaches about 640 MiB. With all three and a 400 MiB container limit, it fills the available memory and fails.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: With the buffer cap enabled, memory remains below 200 MiB and the backup completes.
The container returns memory slightly sooner after the job when mmap is enabled, but its peak is still about 640 MiB.

edges.comment: From c10-c13: ncw requested runtime probes and affected operator linwalth reported raw memory observations. Linwalth also established that the client sends the 290 MB backup in 14 parts with two workers; that unprompted fact enters N2_x as volunteered information. These are measurement probes, not the fix.

question_patterns: What exact `rclone serve s3` command are you running, and what does `rclone version` print inside the container?
Please paste the command line and the version output from the running image.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I run `rclone serve s3 --addr $(SERVES3_ENDPOINT) --vfs-fast-fingerprint --auth-key $(RCLONE_S3PROXY_ACCESS_KEY_ID),$(RCLONE_S3PROXY_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) $(SERVES3_BACKEND):`. Inside the container, `rclone version` reports `rclone v1.75.0-beta.9734.52dd8ad4a.fix-7453-s3-serve-multipart` on Alpine aarch64.

question_patterns: What remote does `SERVES3_BACKEND` actually reference? Please share a redacted configuration.
Is the served remote plain S3, or is another rclone backend layered over it?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Rclone is our encryption proxy. `SERVES3_BACKEND` is `crypted`; that remote has type `crypt` and points to `s3remote:test-bucket`. The underlying `s3remote` is an S3 backend using our Ceph RGW endpoint. We configure it with Kubernetes environment variables rather than an rclone config file.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: `SERVES3_BACKEND` points directly to the plain Ceph S3 remote; there is no crypt layer or other wrapper.
It is still a crypt remote over Ceph S3, but the configuration comes from a mounted config file instead of environment variables.

edges.comment: From c15-c20: ncw asked for the exact command, running version, and remote configuration. Affected operator linwalth supplied the command and explained that the served backend is crypt layered over Ceph RGW S3.

question_patterns: Please test the newly provided candidate against the same encrypted multipart upload and paste any errors.
Can you rerun your backup with this experimental build and report exactly what appears in the log?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The multipart upload fails immediately. The log says `failed to upload chunk 1 with 21501088 bytes: operation error S3: UploadPart, serialization failed: crypt: partEncrypter unsupported seek`, followed by repeated `crypt: overlapping multipart parts - all parts except the last must be the same size` errors.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The encrypted multipart backup completes and memory remains low with no seek or part-size errors.
The same unsupported-seek and unequal-part-size errors occur after the second part rather than the first.

edges.comment: From c21-c24: ncw produced an experimental crypt-compatible candidate and linwalth tested it. The answer preserves the operator's raw log output; the conclusion that the implementation assumptions are incompatible with this part layout remains engineer-side.

question_patterns: Please test the simplified candidate with the same backup and report its memory footprint.
Can you rerun the original backup workload with the new build and tell me what memory usage you observe?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: That worked well. The same backup now creates a much smaller memory imprint.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same backup still reaches about 640 MiB and crashes under the 400 MiB limit.

question_patterns: Could you test a larger upload through the encryption proxy and report whether it completes under realistic client concurrency?
Please exercise the candidate with a multi-gigabyte file and your normal server settings.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I sent a 2 GiB file through the encryption proxy. Client upload concurrency one works, concurrency two like our PG-Barman job also works, and it works with our normal server configuration without `--use-mmap` or `--max-buffer-memory`. The earlier stall only occurred with the client's high concurrency and appears to have been on the client side.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The 2 GiB upload consistently stalls after about 64 parts even with client concurrency one.

question_patterns: After the large upload completes, can you compare the source and destination checksums?
Please verify that the uploaded object has the same MD5 as the original file.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The MD5 checks look good. Both the source and the file read back through `serve s3` report `7e1e0c88057047b9d4912dc409a8e55f`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The upload completes with low memory, but the source and destination MD5 values differ.

edges.comment: From c24-c28: ncw supplied the simplified candidate and linwalth tested the original backup plus a 2 GiB transfer. The affected operator reported lower memory, successful realistic concurrency, and matching checksums. The transient high-concurrency stall was traced by the operator to the client-side test conditions rather than retained as a server failure.

solution.intent: Replace whole-upload multipart retention with the simplified bounded multipart implementation that works through wrapped backends such as crypt, then merge it only after an affected operator verifies memory usage, large-file completion, and data integrity.
solution.concrete_example: Use the simplified `serve s3` multipart implementation rather than keeping every gofakes3 part body alive for the duration of the upload. Validate it through the crypt-over-Ceph setup with the normal backup and a multi-gigabyte upload, require matching checksums, and only then merge it.
solution.inference_hint: The operator supplied the crypt-over-S3 configuration, raw unsupported-seek and unequal-part-size errors, memory observations, transfer results, and checksums. Concluding that the first direct-backend design did not cover crypt, that the crypt-specific attempt assumed an incompatible part layout, and that the simplified implementation is the compatible bounded-memory answer is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: From c24-c29: after the crypt-specific candidate failed, ncw simplified the implementation. Linwalth verified the real encryption-proxy workload, a 2 GiB transfer, realistic client concurrency, and matching MD5 values; ncw then merged the tested implementation. Release scheduling is intentionally not scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the S3-serving library retained every multipart part body in memory, so memory grew with the complete multipart upload.

The diagnosis and fix must be grounded in the collected evidence: the first candidate still reached about 640 MiB, the served destination was crypt over Ceph S3, the crypt-specific candidate produced seek and unequal-part-size errors, and the simplified candidate substantially reduced memory.
Must recommend bounded multipart handling compatible with the reported crypt-wrapped backend rather than relying only on direct multipart interfaces exposed by plain backends.

Must not present `GOGC`, `--use-mmap`, or `--max-buffer-memory` as the actual fix for this defect; the measured workload still reached about 640 MiB and failed under a 400 MiB limit during those probes.
Must not retain the failed crypt-specific candidate as the solution because it produced `partEncrypter unsupported seek` and overlapping-part-size errors.
Must require affected-user verification before declaring resolution, including a realistic large upload and matching source/destination checksums.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical maintainer and infrastructure operator folded into one simulated user side: understands rclone backend interfaces, Go memory controls, Kubernetes containers, S3 multipart behavior, crypt remotes, concurrency tuning, and checksum validation.
persona_hint.communication_style: Collaborative and evidence-driven; shares exact commands, redacted configuration, raw logs, memory measurements, and checksums; readily tests experimental builds and corrects earlier assumptions.
